A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeNIe, with v2 extending the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original GeNIe classification results, noise ablations, oracle-label accuracy, and generated-image analyses in Tables 1–6 and the figures.

after.justification: V2 retains original GeNIe experiments and adds GeNIe-Ada results, expanded noise analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V2 adds GeNIe-Ada to the retained GeNIe procedure. It generates candidates at multiple noise levels, uses classifier embeddings and a target-category example to measure projected semantic changes, and selects the candidate after the largest change (Section 2, Algorithm 1). V1 uses a chosen noise ratio without this adaptive component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate mini-ImageNet, tiered-ImageNet, ImageNet-LT, CUB200, Cars196, Food101, and FGVC-Aircraft under the same classification task families. Additional noise settings and adaptive-method evaluations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator rosters remain, including the long-tailed methods relocated to v2 Table A1. However, v1 Figure 4's UMAP comparison against Img2ImgL, Img2ImgH, and Txt2Img is removed; the replacement embedding analysis examines GeNIe semantic trajectories without these comparators.

E3.justification: New GeNIe-Ada experiments select among noise ratios {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9}, and fine-grained evaluations expand beyond the previous 0.7/0.8 settings. The embedding diagnostic changes from a five-class UMAP comparison to DinoV2/PCA trajectories. Existing benchmark splits, classifier backbones, and stated training settings remain.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the mechanism analysis: Figures 2, 5, and A3 investigate source-to-target semantic transitions supporting adaptive selection, replacing v1's UMAP diversity comparison. Table 4 expands fine-grained noise sensitivity tests, while Table 5 combines the previous noise and oracle-label analyses and adds GeNIe-Ada label-consistency results.

E5.justification: Both report 95% confidence intervals over 600 mini-ImageNet and 1,000 tiered-ImageNet episodes, and average fine-grained accuracy over 100 episodes. New rows follow existing uncertainty-reporting practices; no changed seed counts, repeated-run procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds GeNIe-Ada results throughout the benchmarks, including 52.7% Few-class and 63.1% overall ImageNet-LT accuracy, plus additional fine-grained noise rows. Existing noise-ablation values also change substantially: ResNet-34 mini-ImageNet 5-shot accuracy at r=0.5 changes from 84.66% in v1 Tables 5–6 to 75.80% in v2 Table 5, without a stated setting revision explaining it.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2 introduces the projected embedding-distance definition and formal largest-gap selection criterion underlying GeNIe-Ada. These are limited mathematical additions beyond v1's noise/iteration relationship; neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 contributes GeNIe with a user-chosen noise ratio. V2's abstract and introduction add automatic per-sample noise selection through GeNIe-Ada as an explicit contribution and claim further performance gains. The original hard-negative augmentation contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a semantic-transition explanation for adaptive selection, cautiously hypothesizing that intermediate images lie away from the natural-image manifold. It adds a CutMix/MixUp overfitting interpretation and substantive limitations involving generation latency, unfamiliar domains, and category names. These accompany replacement of v1's UMAP boundary/diversity argument and soft-label future-work proposal.

D1.justification: V2 documents the adaptive candidate grid, a typical maximum of 50 diffusion steps, two-hour long-tailed fine-tuning, and generation times of 4.4/6.7 seconds at r=0.5/0.8 on an RTX 3090. These add technical and cost information; the code link and original training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and limited discussion of adaptive augmentation, including AutoAugment and SAFLEX, feedback-guided synthesis, LANCE, hard-negative work, and faster diffusion models. The UMAP reference disappears with that analysis. The central positioning relative to Boomerang, SDEdit, and other generative augmentation methods remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, and method exposition are rewritten. Related Work moves from before the method to after the experiments, and the appendix is reorganized into numbered subsections. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revision beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout, adds Algorithm 1 and the adaptive-selection schematic, and substantially revises embedding displays. It merges the noise/oracle tables, expands fine-grained rows, and relocates the full long-tailed comparison to the appendix while adding an explicit resolution column to the main comparison.

improvement.justification: GeNIe-Ada provides a concrete, experimentally supported response to v1's noise-selection problem (Algorithm 1; Tables 1–5). Expanded sensitivity analyses and explicit runtime and applicability limitations also improve the paper's usefulness. These gains are qualified by unexplained revisions to existing noise-ablation scores and inconsistent M/n notation in Algorithm 1, supporting a limited overall improvement.
